name: sysctl-kernel-extended
description: Extended kernel / memory / BPF hardening sysctls (kernel-hardening guides).  Absent keys/paths SKIP, never false-fail.

rules.title: net.core.bpf_jit_harden (want 1)
rules.rationale: Hardening the BPF JIT blunts JIT-spray exploitation of the packet filter.

rules.title: dev.tty.ldisc_autoload (want 0)
rules.rationale: Auto-loading TTY line disciplines has been a local-privesc path; pin it off.

rules.title: kernel.core_uses_pid (want 1)
rules.rationale: Tagging core dumps with the PID avoids one process clobbering another's core.

rules.title: vm.unprivileged_userfaultfd (want 0)
rules.rationale: Unprivileged userfaultfd has repeatedly aided use-after-free exploitation.

rules.title: kernel.panic_on_oops (want 1)
rules.rationale: Panicking on an oops fails closed instead of running on in a corrupted state.
rules.fix: sysctl -w kernel.panic_on_oops=1 (note: turns an oops into a reboot).

rules.title: kernel.modules_disabled (want 1)
rules.rationale: Once your modules are loaded, locking further loading blocks a whole class of rootkits.
rules.fix: Set kernel.modules_disabled=1 late in boot (one-way until reboot; breaks hot-plug).

rules.title: kernel.io_uring_disabled (want 1)
rules.rationale: io_uring is a large, exploit-prone surface; disable it where nothing needs it.
rules.fix: sysctl -w kernel.io_uring_disabled=2 (breaks apps that use io_uring).

rules.title: net.ipv4.tcp_sack (want 0)
rules.rationale: Context only — selective ACK has had DoS CVEs (SACK panic); note the state.
